q-95696.name: Question 1
q-95696.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability of getting $12$ defective bolts in a box containing $20$ bolts if the probability that an individual bolt is defective is $0.2.$

II. The probability that a soccer player scores $20$ of $30$ penalties if the probability of scoring each penalty is $0.55.$

III. The probability of getting $9$ fives on $28$ rolls of a $6$-sided die.
q-95696.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=20$ and $p=0.2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =20\cdot 0.2 \\  & =4 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=30$ and $p=0.55.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =30\cdot 0.55 \\  & =16.5 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =30\cdot (1-0.55) \\  & =13.5 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=28$ and $p=\frac{1}{6}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =28\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{14}{3} \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

q-132275.name: Question 6
q-132275.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(85,0.56),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=50).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ | $\,0.6664\,$ | $\,0.6700\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ |
q-132275.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=85$ and $p=0.56.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =85\cdot 0.56 \\  & =47.6 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =85\cdot (1-0.56) \\  & =37.4 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(85)(0.56)=47.6
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(85)(0.56)(1-0.56)=20.94.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(47.6,20.94).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=50).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=50)≈P(49.5\le Y\le 50.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(49.5\le Y\le 50.5) & =P(\frac{49.5-47.6}{\sqrt{20.94}}\le Z\le \frac{50.5-47.6}{\sqrt{20.94}}) \\  & ≈P(0.42\le Z\le 0.63) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.63)-P(Z<0.42) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.63)-P(Z\le 0.42) \\  & =Φ(0.63)-Φ(0.42) \\  & =0.7357-0.6628 \\  & =0.073\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=50)≈0.073.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0758.$

Given that the random variable $X∼B(150,0.48),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=67).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1841\,$ | $\,0.1814\,$ | $\,0.1788\,$ | $\,0.1762\,$ | $\,0.1736\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ | $\,0.2033\,$ | $\,0.2005\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ | $\,0.2297\,$ |
q-132269.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=150$ and $p=0.48.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =150\cdot 0.48 \\  & =72 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =150\cdot (1-0.48) \\  & =78 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(150)(0.48)=72
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(150)(0.48)(1-0.48)=37.44.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(72,37.44).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=67).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=67)≈P(66.5\le Y\le 67.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(66.5\le Y\le 67.5) & =P(\frac{66.5-72}{\sqrt{37.44}}\le Z\le \frac{67.5-72}{\sqrt{37.44}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.90\le Z\le -0.74) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.74)-P(Z<-0.90) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.74)-P(Z\le -0.90) \\  & =Φ(-0.74)-Φ(-0.90) \\  & =0.2297-0.1841 \\  & =0.046\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=67)≈0.046.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0468.$

That is, we can approximate X by Y∼N(11,4.95).

Now, we can estimate the desired probability P(X>10). Using a continuity correction, we have

P(X>10)=P(X≥11)≈P(Y≥10.5).

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(Y≥10.5)=P(Z≥10.5−114.95)≈P(Z≥−0.22)=1−P(Z<−0.22)=1−P(Z≤−0.22)=1−Φ(−0.22)=1−0.4129=0.5871

Therefore,

P(X>10)≈0.587. Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of 0.5914.
